semantic_checklist.paper_evidence: The inspected PDF has the required SHA-256. Theorem 6.3 and equations (6.17)-(6.18) appear in Section 6.3 on printed page 1978, with the proof continuing on page 1979; Algorithm 2 and Theorem 4.1 provide the relevant surrounding context on pages 1954-1956.
semantic_checklist.lean_evidence: The dossier identifies the target as p16_t3_mixed_precision_geometric_convergence and supplies its exact and fully elaborated types.
semantic_checklist.reasoning: The selected source version and passage are the correct ones for P16-T3.

semantic_checklist.paper_evidence: The paper fixes a nonsingular A in R^(n x n), nonzero b, exact x satisfying Ax=b, computed iterates, restart index i, and restart-dependent Arnoldi dimensions k_i.
semantic_checklist.lean_evidence: Lean binds n, arbitrary A and Ainv, one scalar c, two precisions, and two arbitrary Nat-to-Real sequences. It has no b, x, computed iterates, k, k_i, inverse witness, or positive-dimension condition.
semantic_checklist.reasoning: Essential binders and their intended types and roles are absent or replaced by unrelated abstract data.

semantic_checklist.paper_evidence: Theorem 6.3 derives contraction for the errors of the specified computed sequence, and its proof verifies the hypotheses of Theorem 4.1 for every restart i and suitable key dimension k_i.
semantic_checklist.lean_evidence: Lean universally quantifies arbitrary error sequences and then assumes hbackward and hforward, which are the desired one-step contraction statements.
semantic_checklist.reasoning: The core algorithmic conclusion has been moved into hypotheses under a universal abstract-sequence quantifier, changing the quantifier structure and witness dependence.

semantic_checklist.paper_evidence: The paper assumes the problem Ax=b with A nonsingular and b nonzero, the specific unpreconditioned mixed-precision MGS-GMRES implementation, Lambda much smaller than 1, and through Theorem 4.1 the residual/update, inner-solver, and iterate-norm conditions.
semantic_checklist.lean_evidence: Lean assumes only nonnegative c, uLow, and uHigh, an exact multiplier below 1, and the two abstract recurrences. It omits nonsingularity, b nonzero, Ainv=A^{-1}, algorithmic hypotheses, kernel models, and iterate-norm comparison.
semantic_checklist.reasoning: The hypotheses do not characterize the paper's theorem and instead assume its central contraction behavior.

semantic_checklist.paper_evidence: Theorem 6.3 concludes contraction of both actual error notions until the normalized backward error is of order c(n,k)u_high and the relative forward error is of order c(n,k)u_high kappa_F(A).
semantic_checklist.lean_evidence: Lean proves nonnegative abstract floors, q^i <= 1, and conditional geometric bounds for arbitrary sequences. It neither states the actual error formulas nor asserts eventual attainment of either floor.
semantic_checklist.reasoning: Although two abstract sequences are present, the complete paper conclusions are not.

semantic_checklist.paper_evidence: Printed page 1942 defines kappa_F(A) using A^{-1}, defines the two error notions, and explains c(n,k) and the qualitative comparison conventions.
semantic_checklist.lean_evidence: The local definitions reduce to exact products involving arbitrary c and ||A||_F||Ainv||_F, while backwardError and forwardError remain entirely uninterpreted.
semantic_checklist.reasoning: The nontrivial definitions do not recover the paper's condition number, coefficient semantics, or error definitions.

semantic_checklist.paper_evidence: The paper distinguishes exact x and b-Ax_hat from computed x_hat_i and r_hat_i; equations (6.19)-(6.20) explicitly include residual and update perturbations.
semantic_checklist.lean_evidence: There are no exact solution, computed iterate, computed residual, correction, or perturbation binders; only arbitrary real sequences bearing error-like names.
semantic_checklist.reasoning: Exact and computed quantities cannot be distinguished because the quantities themselves were erased.

semantic_checklist.paper_evidence: Section 6.3 specifies Algorithm 2 with M_L^(i)=I, fully stored MGS Arnoldi bases, high-precision lines 3 and 8, and low-precision lines 4-7.
semantic_checklist.lean_evidence: No algorithm, basis, preconditioner, residual, update, Arnoldi process, least-squares solve, correction, or execution-step predicate appears in the target.
semantic_checklist.reasoning: The proposition is an abstract recurrence lemma and has no linkage to mixed-precision restarted MGS-GMRES.

semantic_checklist.paper_evidence: The backward error is ||b-Ax_hat||_2/(||b||_2+||A||_F||x_hat||_2), and the forward error is ||x_hat-x||_2/||x||_2; kappa_F uses Frobenius norms.
semantic_checklist.lean_evidence: Only Frobenius norms of A and arbitrary Ainv occur. Neither vector 2-norm nor either normalized error expression is present.
semantic_checklist.reasoning: The target preserves one matrix norm but omits the norm semantics of both claimed errors.

semantic_checklist.paper_evidence: The paper uses generic low-degree polynomials c(n,k), restart dimensions k_i, and restart index i; separate occurrences of c(n,k) may absorb different constants.
semantic_checklist.lean_evidence: Lean uses one arbitrary scalar c in the contraction and both floors, has no k or k_i, and gives i only the role of an arbitrary sequence index.
semantic_checklist.reasoning: Coefficient dependence, restart-dimension dependence, and algorithmic indexing are not preserved.

semantic_checklist.paper_evidence: Equations (6.19)-(6.20) model high-precision residual and update errors, the proof models casting the residual to low precision, and all inner MGS-GMRES operations use u_low under the standard floating-point model.
semantic_checklist.lean_evidence: uLow and uHigh are merely nonnegative real scalars. No floating-point operations, rounding model, cast, precision assignment, gamma_n term, underflow, overflow, subnormal, NaN, or infinity assumptions occur.
semantic_checklist.reasoning: The high/low precision execution model central to Theorem 6.3 is absent.

semantic_checklist.paper_evidence: Equation (6.17) uses Lambda much smaller than 1; equation (6.18) uses qualitative lesssim bounds. The proof resolves the contraction direction by max(Lambda_1^(i),Lambda_2^(i)) <= Lambda.
semantic_checklist.lean_evidence: Lean replaces smallness by q < 1, uses exact floor comparisons, and assumes exact one-step bounds error(i+1) <= q*error(i).
semantic_checklist.reasoning: The contraction direction agrees with the proof, but the qualitative condition and bounds have been changed into exact relations, with q < 1 substantially weaker than q much smaller than 1.

semantic_checklist.paper_evidence: Printed page 1942 defines forward error and normwise backward error explicitly, and Theorem 6.3 applies those definitions to the computed solution.
semantic_checklist.lean_evidence: backwardError and forwardError are arbitrary functions Nat -> Real with no equations tying them to A, b, x, or computed iterates.
semantic_checklist.reasoning: Names alone do not establish either error notion, so residual, backward, and forward errors are not semantically represented.

semantic_checklist.paper_evidence: Section 2 states that the qualitative notation drops negligible second-order terms and absorbs modest constants into generic low-degree c(n,k).
semantic_checklist.lean_evidence: All products, thresholds, recurrences, and geometric bounds are exact real expressions, with no approximation relation, remainder, or generic-constant interpretation.
semantic_checklist.reasoning: The paper's first-order and hidden-constant conventions are silently erased.

semantic_checklist.paper_evidence: The result concerns real finite-dimensional nonsingular systems solved by one specific unpreconditioned restarted mixed-precision MGS-GMRES algorithm.
semantic_checklist.lean_evidence: The ambient real finite-matrix representation is appropriate, but Lean generalizes to singular and zero-dimensional matrices, arbitrary Ainv, arbitrary sequences, and no algorithm.
semantic_checklist.reasoning: This is not an acceptable specialization or generalization of the benchmark result; it changes the subject of the theorem.

semantic_checklist.paper_evidence: The paper's substantive work proves that the specified numerical algorithm supplies the one-step factors and attainable floors under its conditioning and floating-point assumptions.
semantic_checklist.lean_evidence: The target assumes both one-step recurrences. For example, Ainv=0 and identically zero error sequences satisfy the recurrence implications vacuously with q=0, even for a singular A, and the conclusion becomes elementary.
semantic_checklist.reasoning: The proposition is satisfiable but proves only an induction consequence of the desired result already assumed; it has unintended trivial non-paper instances.

lean_implies_paper.reasoning: The Lean proposition establishes only a generic geometric-sequence lemma after assuming exact one-step contraction. It does not define the actual errors, require Ainv=A^{-1}, characterize the algorithm, or derive contraction from the mixed-precision execution model, so it cannot imply Theorem 6.3.

paper_implies_lean.reasoning: In the weak logical sense, the Lean proposition follows independently of the paper: nonnegative q<1 together with the assumed exact one-step recurrences yields the stated powers by induction. Theorem 6.3 is therefore more than sufficient, but this implication reflects the target's loss of substantive content rather than fidelity.

findings.paper_evidence: Section 6.3 proves the result for unpreconditioned restarted MGS-GMRES with fully stored MGS Arnoldi bases, high-precision residual/update operations, and low-precision inner work.
findings.lean_evidence: The target contains no representation or predicate for the algorithm and assumes hbackward and hforward directly.
findings.impact: The central numerical-analysis result is replaced by an elementary induction lemma that presupposes contraction.

findings.paper_evidence: Equation (6.18) displays the normalized true residual and relative 2-norm solution error.
findings.lean_evidence: backwardError and forwardError are arbitrary real sequences with no defining equations.
findings.impact: The formal result says nothing about actual backward or forward errors of GMRES.

findings.paper_evidence: The paper defines kappa_F(A)=||A||_F||A^{-1}||_F for nonsingular A.
findings.lean_evidence: p16ConditionNumberF multiplies ||A||_F by ||Ainv||_F, but Ainv is unconstrained and A need not be nonsingular.
findings.impact: The contraction and forward-floor scales can be unrelated to conditioning; choosing Ainv=0 makes both vanish.

findings.paper_evidence: The proof uses the high-precision residual and update models (6.19)-(6.20), a low-precision residual cast, and low-precision MGS-GMRES analysis.
findings.lean_evidence: The target treats uLow and uHigh only as nonnegative real numbers.
findings.impact: No conclusion is derived from the mixed-precision execution model that defines the benchmark task.

findings.paper_evidence: The result uses generic c(n,k), restart-dependent key dimensions k_i, and restart iteration i.
findings.lean_evidence: One scalar c is reused everywhere, k and k_i are absent, and i indexes arbitrary sequences.
findings.impact: Dimension dependence, generic-constant variation, and restart semantics are lost.

findings.paper_evidence: The contraction condition is qualitative Lambda much smaller than 1, and the attainable floors use lesssim with suppressed constants and second-order terms.
findings.lean_evidence: Lean uses exact q<1, exact floor thresholds, and exact <= recurrences.
findings.impact: The admissible contraction condition is weakened while the asymptotic error statements are incorrectly converted into exact inequalities.

findings.paper_evidence: The source requires a nonsingular system with nonzero b and invokes Theorem 4.1's numerical-kernel, inner-solver, and iterate-norm assumptions.
findings.lean_evidence: None of these hypotheses appears, and n=0 and singular A are permitted.
findings.impact: The target has many non-paper instances and cannot support the claimed GMRES result.

rationale: The verified PDF states a complete mixed-precision restarted MGS-GMRES theorem about explicitly defined normwise backward and relative forward errors. The Lean target retains only the rough scalar shapes c*uHigh and c*uLow*kappa, but its purported condition number uses an unconstrained Ainv, its errors are arbitrary sequences, and its one-step contraction is assumed rather than derived. It omits the algorithm, actual error definitions, inverse relation, c(n,k), restart dimensions, qualitative comparison conventions, and high/low precision model. The resulting proposition is a valid but substantively much weaker geometric-recurrence lemma, so it is not an acceptable formalization of P16-T3.
